name: dev.morningfold/brief
title: Morning Fold
description: Developer news, read and summarized; search, link summaries, new projects and dependency checks.

tools.name: brief_for_day
tools.description: The brief of one past day within the last 14 days, like todays_brief.

date.description: the day, YYYY-MM-DD, within the last 14 days

topic.description: only stories in this topic, a slug from the topics tool (e.g. go, ai, security)

stack.description: topic slugs to put first (e.g. ["go","databases"]); ignored with a personal token unless given

limit.description: how many stories, at most 30 with a personal token, 5 without

lang.description: language of titles and summaries: en, cs, de, es or fr

tools.name: check_dependencies
tools.description: Check the libraries in a dependency file (Go, JavaScript, Python or Rust: go.mod, package-lock.json, poetry.lock, uv.lock, Cargo.lock and their manifests) against OSV.dev for known vulnerabilities. Pass the whole file. Returns the libraries to update, the version that fixes them and each vulnerability. Nothing about the file is kept.

file.description: the whole contents of a dependency file: go.mod, package.json, package-lock.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, poetry.lock, uv.lock, Pipfile.lock, Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock

project.description: a name for the project, shown in the answer

tools.name: my_dependencies
tools.description: The projects the reader watches on Morning Fold, the known vulnerabilities in the library versions they use (checked every morning), and newer releases of the libraries they use directly (major = may break code). Needs the reader's personal link.

tools.name: new_projects
tools.description: Open-source projects and models gaining the most attention this week (GitHub repositories created in the last month, trending Hugging Face models and Spaces, popular Show HN posts), each with a two-sentence summary and stars gained this week. Optional topic filter; with a date, the projects that first turned up that day; with a query, a search over every project collected so far plus all public GitHub repositories of any age (in github, most starred first, each with a summary). Use it for "what's new in AI agents / Rust / MCP this week" questions, often before articles exist, and to find a repository by what it does ("the grill-me skill for Claude").

topic.description: optional: ai, aitools, go, rust, python, typescript, jvm, devops, databases, security, frontend or devtools

query.description: optional words to search for in every project collected so far (name, description, summary), e.g. 'MCP server' or 'local agents'; best matches first. Also searches all public GitHub repositories (results in github, most starred first), for projects of any age

date.description: optional YYYY-MM-DD within the last 90 days: the projects that first turned up that day, ranked by what they gained since, instead of this week's risers

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find articles from the last two weeks by meaning, not just words, in any language. Returns titles, two-sentence summaries and links.

query.description: what to look for, in plain words, in any language

within.description: day, week or month; default: the last two weeks

limit.description: how many results, at most 30 with a personal token, 5 without

lang.description: language of titles and summaries: en, cs, de, es or fr

tools.name: story
tools.description: One story by id: its summary, the link to the article, and related stories.

id.description: the story id from another tool's results

lang.description: language of titles and summaries: en, cs, de, es or fr

tools.name: summarize_link
tools.description: Read any web page (an article, release note, blog post, README) and get what it is: a two- or three-sentence summary, key points, topics and tags, plus a Morning Fold page to share the summary. Use it when the reader pastes a link and asks what it is or whether it's worth reading. A link Morning Fold already has returns its story_id instead. A few new links a day without a personal token, more with one; links someone already summarized are free.

url.description: the address of the page to summarize (an article, release note, blog post, README...)

lang.description: language of the summary: en, cs, de, es or fr

tools.name: todays_brief
tools.description: Today's developer news: the stories of the last 24 hours with two-sentence summaries, a 1-5 quality score and the links. With a personal token it's sorted for the reader's stack and followed tags.

topic.description: only stories in this topic, a slug from the topics tool (e.g. go, ai, security)

stack.description: topic slugs to put first (e.g. ["go","databases"]); ignored with a personal token unless given

limit.description: how many stories, at most 30 with a personal token, 5 without

lang.description: language of titles and summaries: en, cs, de, es or fr

tools.name: topics
tools.description: The topics stories are sorted into, with the slugs the other tools take.
